headline: Singer Asif Akbar's car shot in Dhaka parking lot
summary: A case has been filed after an unidentified person fired shots at the vehicle of the singer and former BCB director while it was parked.
details: Singer and former Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) director Asif Akbar has filed a case following a shooting incident involving his car in a Dhaka parking lot.
The incident occurred around 4:50 AM on Saturday. Asif Akbar reported hearing a loud noise while in his office, later discovering the rear right door glass of his car was broken.
CCTV footage shows a person arriving in a CNG-powered autorickshaw from the direction of Moghbazar, walking to the Bishal Centre parking lot, and firing a shot at the car's glass.
The shooter then fled the scene in the same autorickshaw. Police have recovered a part of the bullet from the spot.
Asif Akbar estimated the damage to the car's glass to be approximately Tk 20,000.

Hatirjheel Police Station has registered the case. Deputy Commissioner Ibne Mizan of the DMP's Tejgaon Division stated that police are currently analyzing CCTV footage from the scene and surrounding buildings.
Authorities have not yet identified the shooter or made any significant progress in the investigation.
caption:
A shooter fired at singer Asif Akbar's car in a Dhaka parking lot. Who is behind the attack?

Singer and former Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) director Asif Akbar has filed a case following a shooting incident involving his car in a Dhaka parking lot.

The incident occurred around 4:50 AM on Saturday. Asif Akbar reported hearing a loud noise while in his office, later discovering the rear right door glass of his car was broken.

CCTV footage shows a person arriving in a CNG-powered autorickshaw from the direction of Moghbazar, walking to the Bishal Centre parking lot, and firing a shot at the car's glass.

The shooter then fled the scene in the same autorickshaw. Police have recovered a part of the bullet from the spot.

Asif Akbar estimated the damage to the car's glass to be approximately Tk 20,000.

Hatirjheel Police Station has registered the case. Deputy Commissioner Ibne Mizan of the DMP's Tejgaon Division stated that police are currently analyzing CCTV footage from the scene and surrounding buildings.

Authorities have not yet identified the shooter or made any significant progress in the investigation.

headline_marked: State-owned [[Janata Bank website hit by cyberattack]] despite precautions
headline: State-owned Janata Bank website hit by cyberattack despite precautions
summary: The bank's website remains offline as IT teams work to remove spam and repair damage following a precautionary shutdown.
details: The state-owned Janata Bank's website has come under cyberattack, remaining inaccessible to the public as of Sunday morning.
The bank's IT department reported finding signs of two separate cyberattacks and spam in at least two locations on the website.
Both Janata Bank and Bangladesh Bank had taken their websites offline starting Thursday as a precautionary measure following a global cyber alert.
The shutdown followed advice from the European Union's cybersecurity agency regarding two serious security vulnerabilities in PHP, a common programming language.
While Bangladesh Bank restored access to its website on Sunday after a three-day shutdown, Janata Bank has been unable to do so due to the detected attacks.
Other state-owned banks, including Sonali, Agrani, Rupali, and BASIC Bank PLC, remained operational throughout the period.
The bank's IT team is working to fix the damage and hopes to have the site operational by the end of the day.
caption:
A state-owned bank's website was attacked despite being taken offline for safety. How did this happen?

The state-owned Janata Bank's website has come under cyberattack, remaining inaccessible to the public as of Sunday morning.

The bank's IT department reported finding signs of two separate cyberattacks and spam in at least two locations on the website.

Both Janata Bank and Bangladesh Bank had taken their websites offline starting Thursday as a precautionary measure following a global cyber alert.

The shutdown followed advice from the European Union's cybersecurity agency regarding two serious security vulnerabilities in PHP, a common programming language.

While Bangladesh Bank restored access to its website on Sunday after a three-day shutdown, Janata Bank has been unable to do so due to the detected attacks.

Other state-owned banks, including Sonali, Agrani, Rupali, and BASIC Bank PLC, remained operational throughout the period.

The bank's IT team is working to fix the damage and hopes to have the site operational by the end of the day.
